verdicts.reason: A turns the hierarchy upside down: the quote is set tiny and the lime attribution is bigger than the quote. The quote mark has shrunk to a speck, the logo sits alone at top-right, and the small can floats in empty space between the text and the circle. B uses a sensible product-left, quote-right banner layout with the quote clearly dominant and the logo bottom-left as in the original. But the attribution is jammed under the quote, the quote mark floats far above the text, and the can feels small and stranded on the left.

Both inverted hierarchy: the quote is set very small and the attribution in heavier caps outshouts it, and the quote mark is a speck. A also strands the logo at top-right, away from the left text column, and leaves the small can floating in empty space. B at least puts the logo on the text's left edge and makes the can larger and anchored lower, though the can is crowded against the text above it and close to the bottom edge.
